maria: heads up — noticed a weird regression on the HTML template tests after the AWQ/INT8 bakeoff. outputs are missing closing tags or truncating attributes. repro on rw-13b-awq-int8 with small-latency profile. :eyes: kevin: can you paste a failing example and the prompt? any difference vs gptq/int16? maria: reproducible snippet: ``` Input: render a minimal HTML card for a product with image and price Output (awq-int8):

Widget

$9.99

Expected: closing

``` kevin: hmm looks like a tokenization boundary issue — the `` ends up split across tokens after quantization and our prefix-caching combined with batching truncates it. saw similar once with long-prefix packing. sophie: does this only happen on the small-latency deployment profile? any difference if you disable prefix cache or set batch_size=1? maria: tested: batch_size=1 fixes it. disabling prefix cache also fixes it. so it's interaction between batching + prefix cache + awq-int8 kernels. gptq-int8 and fp16 don't show this. sam: can we get a quick bisect across commit/quant config? try AWQ with `chunk_kv=false` and `pack_prefix=false` to confirm. also capture raw tokens. maria: raw tokens attached (trimmed): ```n [5021, 11, 34, 823, 4, 9999, 3, 257, 5020] Decoded: "

Widget

$9.99

" ``` kevin: that token sequence shows boundary token IDs for `/i.jpg\">` overlapping with `

` start. AWQ's quantized attention sometimes reorders logits slightly causing different top-k at tight temp=0.0. With batching and cache the beam is effectively pruned earlier. sophie: mitigation ideas: 1) disable aggressive prefix packing for profiles used by HTML renderers, 2) add a post-generation soft check to close unbalanced tags, 3) run AWQ variant with higher calibration precision or fallback to gptq for HTML-critical routes. sam: ops-bot — can you roll a canary that forces `pack_prefix=false` on `small-latency-8` for 10% traffic? ops-bot: deploy request queued: canary update on profile `small-latency-8` with env `PACK_PREFIX=false` -> rollout 10% starting in 5m. (deploy-id: dply-2024-09-18-773) kevin: also add a quick eval: HTML-close-rate metric over our html-render benchmark. if it drops >0.5% we trigger fallback. maria: running a sweep now across AWQ variants, logging html-close-rate and token-deltas. will paste results in a follow-up thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
